sub: Named after “ṣaff”, the solid battle row, in ayah 4
theme: A call to sincerity: believers must match their words with action, stand firm for Allah’s cause, and not treat their Messenger ﷺ as the Israelites treated Mūsā and ʿĪsā. Allah will complete His light.
story: Revealed in Madinah. No reliable report fixes its date; its content suggests the period after the Battle of Uḥud.
Some Companions said among themselves: if only we knew the deed Allah loves most, we would do it. None dared to ask. Then the Prophet ﷺ called them and recited this whole surah to them.
It gives the answer, striving in Allah’s cause, but first warns against claiming more than you will do. It also warns against treating the Messenger ﷺ as the Israelites treated Mūsā and ʿĪsā.

sections.title: Allah hates saying what you don’t do, loves fighters in solid rows
sections.meaning: Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah. Then a sharp question to the believers: why say what you do not do? Allah hates it greatly. What He loves is those who fight in His cause in rows, like a solid, tightly joined wall.
points: Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah, the Mighty, the Wise
Why do you say what you do not do?
Most hateful to Allah: saying what you don’t do
Allah loves those fighting in His cause in rows, like a solid structure
sections.matters: The Companions wanted the deed Allah loves most. Before telling them, Allah warns against big promises that aren’t kept. Words must match deeds, and the answer, steadfast and united striving, follows at once.
sections.story: Some Companions said, “If we knew the deed Allah loves most, we would do it.” This surah came in reply. Reportedly some then fled at Uḥud; other reports say ayah 2 was about false boasts of battle feats.
explained: The surah opens with sabbaḥa: everything in the heavens and on earth has glorified Allah, the Mighty and Wise. Then it turns to the believers: why do you say what you do not do? Kabura maqtan: it is deeply hateful to Allah when your words run ahead of your actions, like a broken promise.

It covers breaking promises and claiming deeds you never did. Even a sincere plan is best said with “in shāʾ Allāh”. Then comes the answer to their question: Allah loves those who fight for Him in a ṣaff, a row so tight it is bunyān marṣūṣ, a wall with no gaps.
teaches: Don’t promise or claim what you won’t actually do.
Keep your promises; breaking them is hateful to Allah.
Say in shāʾ Allāh when committing to future deeds.
Allah loves unity and discipline in the ranks.
sections.hook: Ayat 2 and 3 both end with the same words, mā lā tafʿalūn (what you do not do). Ayah 4 gives the surah its name: ṣaffan.

sections.title: Mūsā’s people swerve, ʿĪsā foretells Aḥmad; none can blow out Allah’s light
sections.meaning: Mūsā’s people hurt him though they knew he was Allah’s messenger; when they swerved, Allah made their hearts swerve. ʿĪsā confirmed the Torah and gave news of a messenger named Aḥmad, yet when he came they called it magic. They want to blow out Allah’s light, but He will complete it.
points: Mūsā: why do you hurt me, knowing I am Allah’s messenger?
They swerved, so Allah made their hearts swerve
ʿĪsā confirms the Torah and brings news of Aḥmad
When he came with clear proofs, they said: obvious magic
No one is more unjust than one who lies about Allah
They try to blow out Allah’s light; He will make His religion prevail
sections.matters: It warns the believers not to treat their Messenger ﷺ as the Israelites treated Mūsā and ʿĪsā. It also comforts the Prophet ﷺ, who faced similar harm, and promises that no mouth can blow out Allah’s light.
sections.story: No specific incident for ayat 5–7. Reportedly, when revelation paused for forty days, Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf gloated that Allah had put out the light of Muhammad ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ was saddened, and ayah 8 was revealed.
explained: Mūsā asked his people why they hurt him when they knew he was Allah’s messenger. Because they chose to swerve from the truth, Allah made their hearts swerve, a just result of their choice. ʿĪsā then told the Children of Israel he confirmed the Torah before him and brought good news of a messenger after him named Aḥmad.

Aḥmad is a name of the Prophet ﷺ. When he came with clear signs, they called it obvious magic. Who is more unjust than someone who invents lies about Allah while being invited to Islam? They try to put out Allah’s light with their mouths, like blowing at the sun. He will complete it and make His religion prevail.
teaches: Never hurt or disrespect the Messenger ﷺ, as some did to Mūsā.
Turning from truth you know can cost you guidance itself.
Prophets confirm those before them and announce those after.
No effort can extinguish the light Allah has sent.
sections.hook: Two stories start “wa idh qāla”: Mūsā “to his people” (5), ʿĪsā “O Children of Israel” (6). Ayat 8 and 9 both end “though they dislike it.” Page 552 starts at ayah 6.

sections.title: The trade that saves: faith and striving for Paradise; be Allah’s helpers
sections.meaning: Allah offers a trade that saves from painful punishment: believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive with wealth and lives. The profit is forgiveness, gardens and fine homes, plus victory and a near conquest. Then the call: be Allah’s helpers, like ʿĪsā’s disciples, and Allah will support you.
points: Shall I show you a trade that saves from painful punishment?
Believe, and strive with your wealth and your lives
Forgiveness, gardens with rivers, pleasant homes in ʿAdn
And something you love: help from Allah and a near victory
Be Allah’s helpers, as the disciples answered ʿĪsā
Allah supported the believers and they prevailed
sections.matters: Ayah 2 warned against empty words; here is what real commitment looks like and what it earns. It answers the Companions’ question in full, promising reward in both worlds, and holds up the disciples of ʿĪsā as a model.
sections.story: Reportedly these ayat also answer the Companions who wished to know the deed Allah loves most. Another report links ayah 10 to ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn, who asked which trade Allah loves after being told not to renounce the world.
explained: Hal adullukum: shall I guide you? The offer is framed as tijārah, a trade. You invest faith and strive in Allah’s cause with your wealth and yourselves. It beats any worldly deal. The return: sins forgiven, gardens with rivers beneath, and pleasant homes in gardens of ʿAdn, lasting forever. That is the great success.

There is more that you love now: help from Allah and a near victory. Give the believers good news. Then the final call: be anṣār Allāh, helpers of Allah, like the disciples who answered ʿĪsā. Some of the Children of Israel believed and some didn’t, and Allah backed the believers until they came out on top.
teaches: Faith and striving are a trade that never loses.
Give your wealth and yourself for Allah’s cause.
Allah’s reward comes in the Hereafter, and His help in this life.
Be a helper of Allah’s religion, like the disciples of ʿĪsā.
sections.hook: “O you who have believed” comes three times: ayat 2, 10 and 14. ʿĪsā ibn Maryam appears twice: giving news of Aḥmad (6) and calling for helpers (14).

groups.text: Everything in the heavens and earth glorifies Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.
Why say what you don’t do? It is most hateful to Allah.
Allah loves those who fight in His cause in rows, like a solid wall.
Mūsā’s people hurt him though they knew he was a messenger; when they swerved, Allah made their hearts swerve.
ʿĪsā confirmed the Torah and gave news of a messenger named Aḥmad; when he came, they called it magic.
No one is more unjust than one who lies about Allah. Allah will complete His light and make His religion prevail.
A trade that saves: believe and strive with wealth and lives. The reward is forgiveness and eternal gardens.
And something you love now: help from Allah and a near victory. Give the believers good news.
Be Allah’s helpers like ʿĪsā’s disciples. Allah supported those who believed, and they prevailed.

1.explain: Sabbaḥa: has glorified, in the past tense, which conveys certainty. Everything in the heavens and on earth declares Allah free of every flaw. He is al-ʿAzīz, overpowering all, and al-Ḥakīm, wise in creation and command.

2.explain: Why do you say what you do not do? A rebuke for promising or claiming deeds and then not doing them. Keeping a promise is a duty, and breaking it is a sign of hypocrisy.
2.why: Reportedly, Companions said they would give everything if they knew the deed Allah loves most; when tested at Uḥud, some fled. Other reports: men who boasted of battle feats they never did, or hypocrites who promised to fight and stayed behind.

3.explain: Kabura maqtan: maqt is the most intense hatred. Allah strongly hates it when a servant says he will do something and doesn’t. Even a sincere intention is best tied to “in shāʾ Allāh”.

4.explain: Ṣaffan: in a row. Bunyān marṣūṣ: a structure whose parts are pressed tightly together, with no gaps. The Prophet ﷺ would line up his forces in rows before battle. This is the deed Allah loves.
4.why: Reportedly, believers said, “If only we knew the deeds Allah loves most, we would do them,” and this ayah told them. They were then tested at Uḥud.

5.explain: Mūsā asked why they hurt him (tuʾdhūnanī) with words and deeds while knowing he was Allah’s messenger. Zāghū: they swerved from the truth by choice, so Allah made their hearts swerve. He doesn’t guide the defiantly disobedient.

6.explain: ʿĪsā said “O Children of Israel”, not “my people”. He confirmed the Torah before him and gave good news of Aḥmad, a name of the Prophet ﷺ. When the Prophet ﷺ came with clear proofs, they said: plain magic.

7.explain: No one is more unjust than one who invents lies about Allah, giving Him partners or calling His signs magic, while being invited to Islam with clear proof. Allah does not guide people who insist on wrongdoing.

8.explain: Their mouths: their slanders, calling it magic, poetry or fortune-telling. Trying to put out Allah’s light that way is like trying to blow out the sun. Allah will complete His light, however much the disbelievers hate it.
8.why: Reportedly, revelation paused for forty days and Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf told the Jews to rejoice, saying Allah had put out the light of Muhammad ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ was saddened, this ayah came, and revelation continued.

9.explain: He sent His Messenger ﷺ with guidance and the religion of truth, li-yuẓhirahu: to raise it above every other religion by its proofs, and its people too when they hold to it, though the polytheists dislike it.

10.explain: Tijārah: trade. Faith and striving are called a trade because you invest yourself and your wealth and earn Allah’s pleasure and Paradise. This trade saves from a painful punishment.
10.why: Reportedly the Companions had asked for the deed Allah loves most. Another report says ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn, told that Islam has no monasticism, asked which trade Allah loves most, and this came.

11.explain: The trade: believe in Allah and His Messenger, and strive (tujāhidūn) in His cause with your wealth and your lives. It is hard on the soul, yet better for you than any worldly gain, if you only knew.

12.explain: The profit: all sins forgiven, gardens with rivers flowing beneath, and masākin ṭayyibah, pleasant dwellings, in jannāt ʿAdn, gardens of permanent stay no one ever leaves. That is al-fawz al-ʿaẓīm, the great success.

13.explain: Ukhrā tuḥibbūnahā: another blessing you love, in this world. Help from Allah and fatḥ qarīb, a near victory: either Khaybar and Makkah, or the later conquests of Persia and Rome. Give the believers good news.

14.explain: Anṣār Allāh: helpers of Allah’s religion, like ʿĪsā’s ḥawāriyyūn, his sincere disciples. Some Israelites believed, some didn’t. Allah backed the believers until they prevailed, either over the other faction or when the Prophet ﷺ came confirming them.
